issue_context.title: `homectl` cannot unset field `preferredLanguage`
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255.3

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.7.4-arch1-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

homectl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

I expected* the command `homectl` to unset the [field `preferredLanguage`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/docs/USER_RECORD.md#fields-in-the-regular-section) when passing the empty string as argument to its option `--language` as follows:

```Shell
homectl update --language='' -- …
```

*: I expected that not because of any documentation (the [manual page](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/homectl), in particular, does not explain how to unset the mentioned field or even state that it can be done), but because of the [code that handles the option `--language`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/src/home/homectl.c#L2910-L2916). In other words, my expectation may well be wrong; this field could be mandatory.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

Instead, the command `homectl` neither unsets nor modifies the [field `preferredLanguage`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/docs/USER_RECORD.md#fields-in-the-regular-section) when the empty string is passed as argument to its option `--language`.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create a dummy user:

   ```Shell
   homectl create --disk-size=64M --language=en_US.UTF-8 -- foobar
   ```

2. Check the [field `preferredLanguage`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/docs/USER_RECORD.md#fields-in-the-regular-section) has been set properly:

   ```Shell
   homectl inspect --json=pretty --export-format=minimal -- foobar
   ```

   In my system, that command outputs the following:

   ```JSON
   {
           "preferredLanguage" : "en_US.UTF-8",
           "userName" : "foobar",
           "perMachine" : [
                   {
                           "diskSize" : 67108864,
                           "rebalanceWeight" : 0,
                           "matchMachineId" : "b51c83b3827744aeae42a942fa285a51"
                   }
           ],
           "disposition" : "regular",
           "lastChangeUSec" : 1707820248514991,
           "lastPasswordChangeUSec" : 1707820248514991,
           "privileged" : {
                   "hashedPassword" : [
                           "$y$j9T$xHAAKgEL0W/BggM43nXKW0$mht74uMcgD7x4XthgHZDVrrA73nUk.uzblGHWzIohn."
                   ]
           }
   }
   ```

3. Try to unset the [field `preferredLanguage`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/docs/USER_RECORD.md#fields-in-the-regular-section):

   ```Shell
   homectl update --language='' -- foobar
   ```

4. Check whether the [field `preferredLanguage`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/docs/USER_RECORD.md#fields-in-the-regular-section) has been unset:

   ```Shell
   homectl inspect --json=pretty --export-format=minimal -- foobar
   ```

   In my system, that command outputs the following:

   ```JSON
   {
           "preferredLanguage" : "en_US.UTF-8",
           "userName" : "foobar",
           "disposition" : "regular",
           "lastPasswordChangeUSec" : 1707820248514991,
           "perMachine" : [
                   {
                           "diskSize" : 67108864,
                           "rebalanceWeight" : 0,
                           "matchMachineId" : "b51c83b3827744aeae42a942fa285a51"
                   }
           ],
           "privileged" : {
                   "hashedPassword" : [
                           "$y$j9T$xHAAKgEL0W/BggM43nXKW0$mht74uMcgD7x4XthgHZDVrrA73nUk.uzblGHWzIohn."
                   ]
           },
           "lastChangeUSec" : 1707820395590538
   }
   ```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue
